BuildInFunctions.name: ASYMMETRIC_DECRYPT
BuildInFunctions.title: ASYMMETRIC_DECRYPT(algorithm, crypt_str, key_str)
BuildInFunctions.description:
Decrypts an encrypted string using the given algorithm and key string, and returns the resulting plaintext as a binary string. If decryption fails, the result is NULL.

key_str must be a valid key string in PEM format. For successful decryption, it must be the public or private key string corresponding to the private or public key string used with asymmetric_encrypt() to produce the encrypted string. algorithm indicates the encryption algorithm used to create the key.

Supported algorithm values: 'RSA'

BuildInFunctions.name: ASYMMETRIC_DERIVE
BuildInFunctions.title: ASYMMETRIC_DERIVE(pub_key_str, priv_key_str)
BuildInFunctions.description:
Derives a symmetric key using the private key of one party and the public key of another, and returns the resulting key as a binary string. If key derivation fails, the result is NULL.

pub_key_str and priv_key_str must be valid key strings in PEM format. They must be created using the DH algorithm.

BuildInFunctions.name: ASYMMETRIC_ENCRYPT
BuildInFunctions.title: ASYMMETRIC_ENCRYPT(algorithm, str, key_str)
BuildInFunctions.description:
Encrypts a string using the given algorithm and key string, and returns the resulting ciphertext as a binary string. If encryption fails, the result is NULL.

The str length cannot be greater than the key_str length − 11, in bytes

key_str must be a valid key string in PEM format. algorithm indicates the encryption algorithm used to create the key.

Supported algorithm values: 'RSA'

To encrypt a string, pass a private or public key string to asymmetric_encrypt(). To recover the original unencrypted string, pass the encrypted string to asymmetric_decrypt(), along with the public or private key string correponding to the private or public key string used for encryption.

BuildInFunctions.name: ASYMMETRIC_SIGN
BuildInFunctions.title: ASYMMETRIC_SIGN(algorithm, digest_str, priv_key_str, digest_type)
BuildInFunctions.description:
Signs a digest string using a private key string, and returns the signature as a binary string. If signing fails, the result is NULL.

digest_str is the digest string. It can be generated by calling create_digest(). digest_type indicates the digest algorithm used to generate the digest string.

priv_key_str is the private key string to use for signing the digest string. It must be a valid key string in PEM format. algorithm indicates the encryption algorithm used to create the key.

Supported algorithm values: 'RSA', 'DSA'

Supported digest_type values: 'SHA224', 'SHA256', 'SHA384', 'SHA512'

BuildInFunctions.name: ASYMMETRIC_VERIFY
BuildInFunctions.title: ASYMMETRIC_VERIFY(algorithm, digest_str, sig_str, pub_key_str, digest_type)
BuildInFunctions.description:
Verifies whether the signature string matches the digest string, and returns 1 or 0 to indicate whether verification succeeded or failed.

digest_str is the digest string. It can be generated by calling create_digest(). digest_type indicates the digest algorithm used to generate the digest string.

sig_str is the signature string. It can be generated by calling asymmetric_sign().

pub_key_str is the public key string of the signer. It corresponds to the private key passed to asymmetric_sign() to generate the signature string and must be a valid key string in PEM format. algorithm indicates the encryption algorithm used to create the key.

Supported algorithm values: 'RSA', 'DSA'

Supported digest_type values: 'SHA224', 'SHA256', 'SHA384', 'SHA512'

BuildInFunctions.name: CONVERT_TZ
BuildInFunctions.title: CONVERT_TZ(dt,from_tz,to_tz)
BuildInFunctions.description:
Converts a datetime value dt from the time zone given by from_tz to the time zone given by to_tz and returns the resulting value. Time zones are specified as described in Section 5.1.15, “MySQL Server Time Zone Support”. This function returns NULL if any of the arguments are invalid, or if any of them are NULL.

On 32-bit platforms, the supported range of values for this function is the same as for the TIMESTAMP type (see Section 11.2.1, “Date and Time Data Type Syntax”, for range information). On 64-bit platforms, beginning with MySQL 8.0.28, the maximum supported value is '3001-01-18 23:59:59.999999' UTC.

Regardless of platform or MySQL version, if the value falls out of the supported range when converted from from_tz to UTC, no conversion occurs.

Keyword.name: SELECT
Keyword.description: Retrieves data from one or more tables.

Keyword.name: GROUP
Keyword.description: Groups rows based on a specific column in the SELECT statement.
Keyword.example: SELECT department, COUNT(*) FROM employees GROUP BY department;

Keyword.name: HAVING
Keyword.description: Specifies a condition for grouped data in the SELECT statement.
Keyword.example: SELECT department, AVG(salary) AS avg_salary FROM employees GROUP BY department HAVING AVG(salary) > 50000;

Keyword.name: FROM
Keyword.description: Specifies the table from which data is queried.

Keyword.name: ACCESSIBLE
Keyword.description: Specifies that the user must have the privilege to access the table or column.
Keyword.example: GRANT SELECT ON table_name TO user_name;

Keyword.name: ADD
Keyword.description: Adds new columns to an existing table.
Keyword.example: ALTER TABLE employees ADD hire_date DATE;

Keyword.name: ALL
Keyword.description: Used in subqueries to allow comparison with all values in the result set.
Keyword.example: SELECT product_name FROM products WHERE price > ALL (SELECT price FROM products WHERE category_id = 1);

Keyword.name: ALTER
Keyword.description: Modifies an existing database object such as a table or view.
Keyword.example: ALTER TABLE employees RENAME COLUMN old_column_name TO new_column_name;

Keyword.name: ANALYZE
Keyword.description: Collects statistics and stores them in the data dictionary.

Operators.name: AND
Operators.description: A logical operator that returns true if both operands are true.
Operators.example: SELECT column1, column2 FROM table_name WHERE column1 > 10 AND column2 < 5;

Operators.name: BETWEEN
Operators.description: A keyword used to filter rows based on a range of values.
Operators.example: SELECT * FROM table_name WHERE column1 BETWEEN 10 AND 50;

Operators.name: IN
Operators.description: A keyword used to compare a value against a list of values.
Operators.example: SELECT * FROM table_name WHERE column1 IN (value1, value2, value3);

Operators.name: LIKE
Operators.description: A keyword used to perform pattern matching.
Operators.example: SELECT * FROM table_name WHERE column1 LIKE 'abc%';

Operators.name: NOT
Operators.description: A logical operator that negates the following condition.
Operators.example: SELECT * FROM table_name WHERE NOT column1 = 'value';

Operators.name: OR
Operators.description: A logical operator that returns true if at least one operand is true.
Operators.example: SELECT column1, column2 FROM table_name WHERE column1 > 10 OR column2 < 5;

Operators.name: IS
Operators.description: A keyword used to compare a value against NULL.
Operators.example: SELECT * FROM table_name WHERE column1 IS NULL;

Operators.name: NULL
Operators.description: A special value representing 'no value' or 'unknown'.
Operators.example: SELECT * FROM table_name WHERE column1 IS NULL;

Operators.name: INTERSECT
Operators.description: A set operator used to combine the results of two or more SELECT statements, returning only the common rows.
Operators.example: SELECT column1 FROM table1 INTERSECT SELECT column1 FROM table2;

Operators.name: UNION
Operators.description: A set operator used to combine the results of two or more SELECT statements, returning all rows without duplicates.
Operators.example: SELECT column1 FROM table1 UNION SELECT column1 FROM table2;

Operators.name: INNER
Operators.description: A keyword used in a JOIN clause to specify that only matching rows are returned.
Operators.example: SELECT * FROM table1 INNER JOIN table2 ON table1.column = table2.column;

Operators.name: JOIN
Operators.description: A keyword used to combine rows from two or more tables based on a related column.
Operators.example: SELECT * FROM table1 JOIN table2 ON table1.column = table2.column;

Operators.name: LEFT
Operators.description: A keyword used in a JOIN clause to specify that all rows from the left table are returned along with matching rows from the right table.
Operators.example: SELECT * FROM table1 LEFT JOIN table2 ON table1.column = table2.column;

Operators.name: OUTER
Operators.description: A keyword used in a JOIN clause to specify that all rows from both tables are returned, with NULL values in non-matching rows.
Operators.example: SELECT * FROM table1 FULL OUTER JOIN table2 ON table1.column = table2.column;

Operators.name: RIGHT
Operators.description: A keyword used in a JOIN clause to specify that all rows from the right table are returned along with matching rows from the left table.
Operators.example: SELECT * FROM table1 RIGHT JOIN table2 ON table1.column = table2.column;
